## Definition

The **experimental condition** (or treatment condition) is where the independent variable of interest is present or applied. Participants in this condition receive the treatment being tested.

## Characteristics

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Treatment present | Active ingredient/manipulation applied |
| Test group | Used to test the hypothesis |
| Compared to control | Evaluated against baseline |

## Examples

| Study | Experimental Condition |
|-------|----------------------|
| Drug trial | Receives active medication |
| Caffeine study | Drinks caffeinated coffee |
| Therapy evaluation | Receives CBT therapy |
| Teaching method | Uses new teaching approach |

## Experimental vs. Control

```
Research: Does caffeine improve alertness?

Experimental Condition     Control Condition
        │                        │
        ▼                        ▼
   Caffeinated              Decaffeinated
     coffee                   coffee
        │                        │
        ▼                        ▼
   Measure                   Measure
   alertness                 alertness
        │                        │
        └────────┬───────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
              Compare
```

## Multiple Experimental Conditions

Studies can have several experimental conditions:

| Condition | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Control | Placebo (0mg caffeine) |
| Experimental 1 | Low dose (50mg caffeine) |
| Experimental 2 | Medium dose (100mg caffeine) |
| Experimental 3 | High dose (200mg caffeine) |

## DataLab Connection

At the **Frontal Lob** station, the incongruent trials represent the experimental condition where interference is present, while congruent trials serve as the control.
